title: Minimal change disease and FSGS

steps.tx: Classic **Minimal change disease** (**MCD**) exhibits entirely normal glomerular architecture on routine light microscopy alongside completely negative immunofluorescence staining. Definitive diagnosis rests exclusively upon ultrastructural electron microscopy, which demonstrates diffuse, uniform effacement and retraction of visceral epithelial **podocyte foot processes** across the intact basement membrane.

vis.caption: Diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes on electron microscopy (StewardMD).

steps.tx: First-line remission induction therapy for adult minimal change disease utilizes high-dose oral **prednisone** at a dosage of **1** mg/kg/day (maximum **80** mg/day, or **2** mg/kg alternate days) maintained for at least **4** weeks following complete proteinuria resolution, before initiating an extended taper over **6** months to prevent relapses.

left.title: Clinical Sequence
points: Slow taper over 6 months to prevent relapse

steps.tx: In patients exhibiting frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent courses, second-line immunosuppressive strategies incorporate oral **cyclophosphamide** at **2** mg/kg/day for **8** to **12** weeks. Alternatively, calcineurin inhibitors including **tacrolimus** or targeted B-cell depletion using the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody **rituximab** provide durable steroid-sparing disease control.

left.title: Cyclophosphamide Therapy
points: Monitors for leukopenia and gonadal toxicity

steps.tx: Primary **focal segmental glomerulosclerosis** (**FSGS**) is postulated to arise from a circulating permeability factor, such as soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (**suPAR**), which disrupts podocyte alphavbeta3 integrin signalling. This circulating mediator triggers sudden, profound nephrotic syndrome with extensive foot process effacement and high risk of post-transplant recurrence.

vis.caption: Segmental capillary collapse, hyalinosis, and podocyte detachment in FSGS (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Under the standardized **Columbia classification**, light microscopy categorizes FSGS into five distinct morphological variants: **collapsing** variant carrying the poorest renal survival, the **tip** lesion associated with excellent glucocorticoid responsiveness, the cellular variant, the perihilar variant reflecting hemodynamic stress, and not otherwise specified (**NOS**).

steps.tx: Secondary adaptive non-genetic FSGS stems from maladaptive **glomerular hyperfiltration** and structural hypertrophy occurring in states of severely reduced nephron mass, such as **unilateral renal agenesis**, surgical ablation, or severe **morbid obesity**. Patients classically present with indolent, subnephrotic proteinuria and normal serum albumin without generalized edema.

left.title: Adaptive Hemodynamic FSGS
points: Managed with RAAS and SGLT2 inhibitors

steps.tx: Homozygous or compound heterozygous carriage of **APOL1** risk alleles designated **G1** and **G2** in individuals of recent African descent confers marked genetic susceptibility to hypertensive **nephrosclerosis**, collapsing FSGS, and **HIVAN**. APOL1 variant proteins form cytotoxic cation pores in podocyte membranes, inducing lysosomal swelling and cell death under inflammatory stress.

steps.tx: The dual endothelin A and angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonist **Sparsentan** significantly reduces proteinuria in patients with biopsy-proven primary FSGS. Demonstrating superior antiproteinuric efficacy compared with active **irbesartan** monotherapy in the pivotal **DUPLEX** randomized clinical trial, sparsentan provides combined hemodynamic nephroprotection and podocyte cytoskeletal stabilization.
